diagnosis.llm_reason: The physician discharge diagnosis is nephrolithiasis (right, ureteropelvic junction, complex, >2 cm stone burden), i.e., an obstructing renal/ureteral calculus. None of the five ranked differentials names a urinary calculus or obstructive uropathy. Rank 1 acute kidney injury, rank 2 anemia, rank 3 hematuria, rank 4 nephrostomy tube site pain, and rank 5 fever are all complications, symptoms, or sequelae that may accompany obstructing stone disease, but none is the same principal condition. Hematuria and nephrostomy-related pain are symptom-level findings, not the underlying stone disease; AKI is a distinct renal functional diagnosis.
